description: A lift-up side table: push the handle down to release the push-push latch; the gas strut lifts the carriage and the doors open. Push it back down to close and latch. Everything moves by its forces: your hand, the strut, the weights, friction, the latch cam and the dock pins. The door linkage follows the CAD mates.
notes: How it moves. Below lift 0 only the carriage moves (latch overtravel): the carrier stands on its slot floor. From 0 to 29.1 the carrier rises with the carriage; then it stops and the doors swing open, done by lift 76. Pad A (torch charging) touches the dock pins when latched; pad B (LED strip) at lift 200.
Strut: GS535-type gas strut, 100 N, lower ball stud on an upright bracket; fully extended at lift 200, so it is the open stop.
Cables: a USB module and two bridge rectifiers sit in an electronics bay in the underside of the upper. Pad B wires run in a bore up the rail upright; pad A wires rise through two curved holes.
This example is a snapshot of a real design project (side table S3, 2026-10-31). Its files are CC BY-NC 4.0: see LICENSE in this folder.
